coinComparisonHint: Readings that exist per coin, sorted by return. Order flow and the signal lab stay out of comparison mode because they would mix different assets.
correlationHint: Correlation of price changes over the period. Near +1 the coins rise and fall together; near -1 they move in opposite directions.
correlationWeakHint: An uncoloured cell is one whose coefficient is indistinguishable from zero at the available sample size: the number exists, but it does not support a reading. Hover to see how many points back each pair.
correlationWeak: indistinguishable from zero at this sample size
anomalyVariationTitle: Unusual change: {{sigmas}}σ from the period average
normalizationBase100Hint: Relative performance — every coin starts at 100
signalLabHint: What happened AFTER each signal, against the baseline rate. Dimmed rows are those whose confidence interval contains the baseline: the number exists, but is indistinguishable from chance at this sample size.
signalLabHoldoutWarning: The table ranks {{total}} signals by largest shift, and that pushes to the top exactly what chance favours most: at 95% confidence, every row has a 5% chance of standing out on its own. So the most recent {{fracao}}% of the window is held back — the validation column is the only one that took no part in the ranking. Both deltas are measured against the baseline rate of their own slice, shown in the baseline row.
signalNotSignificant: The confidence interval contains the baseline rate: indistinguishable from chance at this sample size
chartModeCandleHint: OHLC candles — open, high, low and close
simulationHint: What if you had traded this signal? Entry happens at the open of the candle after the signal, and costs are charged on both legs.
simulationOpenAtEnd: {{count}} trade(s) still open when the window ended. They move the equity curve, but they are neither a win nor a loss — the metrics count the {{concluidas}} that reached an outcome.
simulationNoTrades: No trades in the period with these parameters.
simulationSmallSample: Fewer than {{count}} closed trades: the numbers exist, but they do not support a conclusion.
simulationGaps: {{count}} gap(s) in collection within the period. Trades that would cross a gap were refused, and open positions were closed at the last known price.
simulationHoldoutHint: The most recent {{fracao}}% of the window is held back. Tune the parameters against the tuning column; the validation column shows how that holds up on the stretch you did not use to choose.
simulationRankingHint: All {{total}} available entry rules, with the SAME exit and the SAME cost, ranked by how much they beat buy & hold over the TUNING stretch. Click a name to simulate that rule in detail above.
simulationRankingWarning: Picking the best of {{total}} is overfitting by construction: the more rules you test, the likelier one looks good by chance. The table is ordered by TUNING — the stretch the rule was picked on. Validation took no part in the ordering, and the drop between the two is what separates a finding from luck.
simulationHoldoutSmall: Fewer than {{minimo}} trades in this stretch: the number exists, but the sample does not support a conclusion.
simulationTooShort: Window too short to hold back a validation split.
simulationLoadError: Could not load the simulation series. The rest of the dashboard is unaffected.
simulationWindowShort: {{pedidos}} days were requested, but the collection covers {{dias}}: trades, alpha and the validation stretch refer to the period that exists, not the one asked for.
simulationMoreRulesHint: trend, confirmation, exit on signal, cost and risk
simulationVerdictBehind: It trailed simply holding the asset by {{diferenca}} p.p.
simulationVerdictAhead: It beat buy & hold by {{diferenca}} p.p.
simulationCaveatValidation: Validation rests on {{count}} trade(s), fewer than the {{minimo}} needed to support a conclusion.
simulationOutOfSampleSub: alpha in the most recent {{fracao}}% of the window
simulationOutOfSampleNone: no trades in the reserved stretch
simulationTrustHint: Return interval, reliance on the best trades, break-even cost, risk and full validation
simulationTrustPush: Does the result survive a push?
simulationRiskNeedsStop: Sizing divides the risk by the stop distance: set a stop to use this field.
simulationNoExitRule: With no exit rule the position would never close. Pick a holding period, a stop, a target or an exit signal.
simulationVerdictChance: It beat {{percentil}}% of random entries drawn the same number of times.
simulationVerdictChanceWeak: It is indistinguishable from random entries: it beat only {{percentil}}% of them, below the {{limiar}}% threshold.
simulationVerdictCiPositive: The return's confidence interval lies entirely above zero.
simulationVerdictCiNegative: The return's confidence interval lies entirely below zero.
simulationVerdictCiZero: But the return's confidence interval includes zero.
simulationVerdictValidation: In the stretch reserved for validation, alpha was {{valor}}.
simulationPriceChartHint: Click a marker on the chart or the entry price in the table to see the candles around that trade.
simulationExcursionHint: Each point is a completed trade: horizontally, how far it moved against (or in favor of) the position before closing; vertically, how it ended. Click a point to see it on the chart.
simulationExcursionWinners: {{fracao}}% of the {{count}} winners pulled back at most {{valor}} before closing.
simulationExcursionLosers: Half of the {{count}} losers reached {{valor}} in favor before turning.
simulationMonthlyHint: Strategy versus buy & hold, month by month, in UTC. An alpha that all comes from a single month describes that month, not a rule.
simulationMonthlySummary: Beat buy & hold in {{vencidos}} of {{total}} months.
simulationSensitivityHint: Alpha in the TUNING stretch for each stop and target combination, with the same entry, holding period and cost. A result that only exists in one cell surrounded by red is an overfitting spike; a whole green region is more robust. Click a cell to apply it.
simulationSensitivityAtr: The grid uses fixed stops. Clicking a cell swaps the volatility stop for that row's fixed one.
simulationSensitivityNeighbors: Of the {{total}} neighbors of the current configuration, {{concordam}} have alpha of the same sign.
simulationRankingLuck: Expected luck: the best of {{total}} RANDOM signals reaches {{mediana}} alpha in tuning, and {{p95}} in 5% of draws. Rows marked ▲ exceed that second number.
simulationRankingAboveLuck: Above what the best of {{total}} random signals reaches 95% of the time.
simulationJournalHint: Save the current configuration to compare it with others. It stays in this browser only, per coin.
simulationJournalFull: The journal holds {{max}} configurations: remove one to save another.

ajuda.atr: How far the price typically travels within a candle. Useful to size distances by measured volatility instead of by guesswork; it indicates no direction.
ajuda.colIntervalo: The range where the true rate probably lies, at 95% confidence. If the baseline rate fits inside it, the signal is indistinguishable from chance.
ajuda.colOcorrencias: How many times this signal appeared in the period. The smaller the number, the less can be concluded.
ajuda.colRetornoMedio: Average price return over the chosen horizon, counting only the times this signal appeared.
ajuda.colTaxaAlta: Of the times the signal appeared, how often the price rose within the chosen horizon.
ajuda.colVsBase: How much the signal shifts the up rate compared with not filtering at all. This is the number that answers whether it is useful.
ajuda.colAjusteSinal: The signal shift over the slice the table was ranked on, against the baseline rate of that same slice. In parentheses, how many times the signal occurred there.
ajuda.colValidacaoSinal: The same calculation over the held-back slice, which took no part in the ranking and did not feed the tuning indicators. If the shift shrinks or flips sign here, the row describes the stretch of past it was picked from, not the market.
ajuda.deltaAcumulado: Volume bought minus sold, accumulated over the chosen period. Positive means more buying than selling. When the price rises and this line does not follow, the rally is not backed by real buying.
ajuda.drawdown: Had you bought at the worst moment of the period, this is how far it would have fallen to the bottom. It measures the swing you would have had to endure, not the final result.
ajuda.faixaBollinger: Blue band: 20-candle moving average with 2 standard deviations on each side. The price usually spends most of its time inside it.
ajuda.fearGreed: Crypto market sentiment index, from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed). It comes from an external source and is the same for every coin.
ajuda.linhaVwap: Purple dashed line: the VWAP, volume-weighted average price accumulated since the start of the period.
ajuda.melhorPior: The candle that rose the most and the one that fell the most in the period. Gives a sense of the extremes seen here.
ajuda.pressaoCompradora: Of the quantity traded right now, how much came from buyers. Above 50% there was more buying than selling. The figure below is the period average, so you can tell whether the current reading is routine or a departure.
ajuda.retornoAcumulado: How much the price moved from the first to the last candle in the period. Not what you would have made: that depends on when you entered and exited.
ajuda.rsi: Compares the strength of gains against losses over the last 14 candles. Above 70 is usually called overbought and below 30 oversold, but check the Signal Lab to see whether that actually precedes anything.
ajuda.sinalBandaInferior: The price closed below the lower band coming from inside it.
ajuda.sinalBandaSuperior: The price closed above the upper Bollinger band coming from inside it.
ajuda.sinalDivAltista: The price fell over the last candles, but accumulated selling flow did not follow.
ajuda.sinalDivBaixista: The price rose over the last candles, but accumulated buying flow did not follow.
ajuda.simAlvo: Distance, in %, from the entry where the position closes in profit. Left blank, there is no target and the exit is left to the stop or the time limit.
ajuda.simBuyHold: What buying at the start of the period and doing nothing else would have returned. It is the yardstick: a strategy returning less than this charged work and risk without delivering anything in exchange. Computed without cost, on purpose, so the comparison is not made easy.
ajuda.simCusto: Fee charged on each leg of the trade — one on entry, one on exit. The 0.1% default is the spot taker fee.
ajuda.simCustoTotal: How much of the trading went out as fees. Comparing this number against the return is what separates a profitable strategy from one that merely moves money around.
ajuda.simDrawdown: The largest fall of simulated capital from a peak, measured candle by candle rather than only at each trade close. It is the size of the worst moment you would have sat through.
ajuda.simHoldout: The most recent stretch of the window is held back and takes no part in tuning. If the result collapses there, the parameters were picked to fit the past you looked at, not because they describe anything.
ajuda.simStopAtr: Fixed uses the same distance for the whole period. By volatility sizes each entry from that candle's ATR: twice it, capped between 1% and 10%. A 2% stop is tight on an asset swinging 5% a day and loose on one swinging 0.5% — the ATR fits the distance to what the asset was actually doing at that moment. Trailing starts like the volatility stop and then follows the price: after each closed candle it moves up (long) or down (short) to the same distance from the best price reached, and never moves back.
ajuda.simRanking: Each row is the same exit rule applied to a different entry signal. Alpha measures how much the strategy beat simply holding the asset; negative means trading gave more work and less money. The validation column repeats the calculation on the stretch that took no part in the ranking, with the trade count in parentheses.
ajuda.simSharpe: How much return the strategy delivered per unit of risk, annualized and measured candle by candle over the equity curve. Above 1 is usually considered good, but read it alongside exposure: a strategy that sits out of the market most of the time has a flat curve, and a flat curve inflates Sharpe without the strategy being any better. Risk-free rate treated as zero.
ajuda.simStop: Distance, in %, from the entry where the position closes at a loss. When a candle touches both stop and target, the simulation assumes the stop: the candle does not record which came first.
ajuda.simSaidaSinal: Closes the position when the chosen signal appears — at the open of the next candle, like the entry, because the signal is only known at the close of the candle that produced it. Works alongside the other exits: whichever happens first closes the position.
ajuda.simTendencia: Only lets the rule enter when the close of the signal candle is above (or below) the 50-candle moving average. While the average does not exist yet, at the start of the series, the filter rejects. Applies to every row of the comparison.
ajuda.simConfirmacao: Requires a second signal to have appeared on the entry signal's candle or on one of the two before it. More conditions make the rule more specific — and easier to fit to the past by chance.
ajuda.simRisco: Instead of committing all the capital, each trade uses the fraction that makes the stop cost this percentage of capital. A 2% stop with 1% risk uses half the capital. Never above 100%: there is no leverage.
ajuda.simAcaso: The same rule — exit, cost, direction and filter — with the entries swapped for randomly drawn candles, as many times as the signal appeared. The percentage says how many draws the strategy beat. It separates the value of the signal from the effect of the exit and of the market's direction. The threshold starts at 95 and rises as more configurations are tested.
ajuda.simIc: Resamples the completed trades, with replacement, a thousand times, and compounds the capital of each resample. The interval holds 95% of those results. Wide and crossing zero means that, with these trades, winning and losing are equally consistent with what was seen.
ajuda.simSemMelhores: The compounded return without the best-performing trades. If it collapses, the result depends on a few events, not on a behavior that repeats.
ajuda.simEquilibrio: The fee per leg at which alpha reaches zero, recalculating the same trades. Below 0.05% the rule only exists for those paying professional-account fees.
ajuda.simTentativas: How many distinct configurations you have simulated for this coin, in this browser. Each one is a test, and whoever tests many finds one that looks good by chance. That is why the chance threshold rises with the count (Bonferroni correction). Changing only the cost does not count.
ajuda.simSubmerso: How far the capital sits below the best value it has had, candle by candle. The drawdown card gives the worst moment; this band shows how long and how often the capital stayed underwater. The dashed line is buy & hold.
ajuda.simExcursao: MAE is how far the trade moved against the position before closing; MFE, how far it moved in favor. Both in % of the entry price, before costs. Looking at them shows what a stop or a target would have done to the trades that existed, without testing distance after distance.
ajuda.simMensal: Each month starts where the previous one ended, in capital and price, so the product of the months rebuilds the total. A month with no trades counts: staying out is a decision of the rule. Months less than 90% covered are faded.
ajuda.simSensibilidade: Each cell is the same rule with another stop and target, measured only in the tuning stretch. Validation is left out on purpose: showing it would turn the reserved stretch into one more place to choose from.
ajuda.simDiario: Saved configurations stay in your browser, per coin, with the result from the moment they were saved. Saving the same configuration again updates its row.
ajuda.simJanela: The simulation fetches its own 180-day series, independent of the dashboard filters: changing the period above does not change the result here.
ajuda.sinalDoji: Open and close in practically the same place. The price moved and came back, with no resolution.
ajuda.sinalEstrela: Mirror of the hammer: long upper shadow, the price rose during the candle and was pushed back.
ajuda.sinalMartelo: Small body with a long lower shadow: the price fell during the candle and was pushed back. On its own it does not mean reversal; what came before is what gives it meaning.
ajuda.sinalMarubozu: Large body with almost no shadows: the move went one way from start to finish of the candle.
ajuda.sinalTicketAlto: Candle where the average value per trade exceeded 2x the median: few large orders rather than many small ones.
ajuda.sinalVariacaoAtipica: Candle whose change exceeded 2 standard deviations from the period average.
ajuda.sinalVolumeAtipico: Candle whose volume exceeded 3x the period median.
ajuda.sinalVwapBaixo: The price closed below the VWAP coming from above it.
ajuda.sinalVwapCima: The price closed above the VWAP coming from below it.
ajuda.taxaAlta: Share of candles that closed above their own open. Near 50% is normal market behaviour and indicates no trend.
ajuda.ticketMedio: Average dollar value of each executed trade. A low ticket with high volume means many small participants; a high ticket means few large orders.
ajuda.velas: Each candle shows the open, high, low and close. Green closed above the open; red, below.
ajuda.volatilidade: How much the price swung inside the current candle, as a percentage. The comparison with the median tells you whether this moment is busier than the period normal.
ajuda.vwap: The period average price weighted by the volume traded at each moment. It is the benchmark professional desks use to judge whether a purchase was expensive or cheap.
